C0.quote: selecting a committee of representatives for a large population
C0.note: Committee selection rule (Expanding Approvals) from ranked ballots; metric distortion and proportional representation. Eligible, though also framed for clustering.

C1.quote: selects an (α, γ)-proportionally representative committee R of size k
C1.note: Main results are approximation guarantees (representativeness, distortion) for a polynomial algorithm, plus lower bounds. Primary WD (approximation of proportional representation/distortion). AX is weak: core/fairness property satisfaction. Doubt between AL and WD resolved by listing order only if equal; here WD judged larger share.

C2.1.quote: refer to it as the rankedchoice profile

C2.2.quote: Voters rank candidates by non-decreasing distances
C2.2.note: Rankings induced by metric distances; also cardinal metric model discussed for known distances (not main).

C2.3.quote: Voters rank candidates by non-decreasing distances, so c ≻v c' implies
C2.3.note: Distances/metric positions are held attitudes of voters.

C2.4.quote: the voters are assumed to rank the candidates by non-decreasing distance
C2.4.note: Rankings are assumed to be consistent with distances and rule applied directly; no statement about submission/reporting or strategic misreport.

C3.2.note: Rankings assumed consistent with distances, but no statement about voters submitting held attitude/sincerity.

C4.1.quote: We say that a pseudo-metric d is consistent with the rankedchoice profile
C4.1.note: Metric model defines costs/distances consistent with rankings; distortion and costs used for voters.

C5.1.quote: all sufficiently large coalitions of voters are well represented
C5.1.note: Proportional representation, core fairness, and metric distortion are evaluation criteria.

C5.2.quote: worst-case loss in the objective function due to the lack of information
C5.2.note: Evaluated on distances in a metric consistent with rankings; defined separately from ranking input (distortion).

VOT.note: Voters are inputs; no action modelled as agent choice beyond fixed rankings.

ORG.note: Rule is analysed; no organiser choice modelled.

DES.note: Designer objective not modelled as agent.
